pending_commit.commit_message: CHORMIUM: mac80211: combine airtime deficit and queue limit check Combine the airtime deficit and queue limit check into ieee80211_txq_airtime_limit_check(), so the airtime fairness is also enforced on packet release triggered by ath10k_htt_txrx_compl_task(). cryptohome: Add new commandline features for cryptohome commandline tool. To add new data restore key, simply type: cryptohome --action=add_data_restore_key --user=your_user_name Then type in your password, wait for a few second, then the hex string of data restore key will be displayed if authenticated. To build authentication, testers can use switch "--restore_key_in_hex" to provide data restore key in HexString, for instance if testers type: cryptohome --action=check_key_ex --user=your_user_name --restore_key_in_hex=0123456789ABCDEF Cryptohome will use restore key in AuthorizationRequest and check if it can be authenticated. To mass remove keys, users need to provide exempt key labels. Every other keyset whose label is not in exempt_key_labels will be removed. For instance, if users have four keysets which are labeled as "l1", "l2", "l3" and "l4", say if they want to delete l1 and l2 and keep l3 and l4, they should type: cryptohome --action=mass_remove_keys --user=your_user_name --exempt_key_labels=l3,l4 After authenticated, l1 and l2 will be removed. BUG=chromium:945057 TEST=Flash image to physical device and use cryptohome command line to test. Change-Id: Idb49cb2a3a314307f65dec41d146a8293bba4fc2 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1684356 Tested-by: Shaojiang Zhong <sjzhong@google.com> Commit-Ready: Shaojiang Zhong <sjzhong@google.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Ryo Hashimoto <hashimoto@chromium.org>

firmware_IntegratedU2F: Run test while logged in. The new U2F implementation reads files from the current user's home dir, so testing it requires a user to be logged in. A follow up change will actually start testing thw new implementation. This change replaces the login_LoginSuccess test (which logs in and then out immediately) with autologin.py (which does not). This allows U2FTest to be run while logged in. The test logs out manually at the end of the run by restarting the UI. Internally, the autologin.py script logs in using the same method as the login_LoginSuccess test. This change also removes some calls to clear TPM, as they are not necessary to run the test. UPSTREAM: drm/i915/skl: Fix has_ipc on skl and document WaDisableIPC. According to Spec for SKL+: "Isochronous Priority Control. If enabled, Display sends demoted requests once the transition watermark is reached. If transition watermark is not enabled, Display sends demoted requests when the display buffer is full." The commit 'e57f1c02155f ("drm/i915/gen9+: Add has_ipc flag in device info structure")' introduced that as gen9+ but missing many SKL Skus. I believe the reason for that is Spec also mentions workarounds for SKL-ALL: "IPC (Isoch Priority Control) may cause underflows WA: Do not enable IPC in register ARB_CTL2" It seems lame to add the feature and forever disable it, but it will avoid a mistake of enabling it when we are reorganizing the feature definitions on i915_pci.c later. It will also allow us to probably extend that workaround for other platforms. dlcservice: Install completion determined from DBus signal When update_engine signals its listeners of a status update, dlcservice is one of those listeners. Previously, dlcservice determined that update engine was done installing DLC(s) based off that fact that dlcservice held onto the DLC(s) it sent over to update_engine and that update_engine sent a status with operation IDLE. Now, a more solidified method of letting update_engine, who knows whether an install or update is in progress, indicate this field through `is_install` within |update_engine::StatusResult| is used by dlcservice to determined an install completion.
